claims.text: OrdersController.Create reads the caller id from sub, maps request items to OrderItem, calls orderService.PlaceOrderAsync, and returns CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order)).

PlaceOrderAsync throws ArgumentException on an empty list, builds an Order with Status "new", calls repository.AddAsync then SaveChangesAsync, then notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"), and returns the Order.

EfOrderRepository.AddAsync calls db.Orders.AddAsync (staging the entity), and SaveChangesAsync calls db.SaveChangesAsync, which sends the INSERT; PostgreSQL assigns the id and EF Core copies it back to order.Id.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: EfOrderRepository.cs:16-18; EF Core docs: saving data, generated values

claims.text: CreatedAtAction answers 201 Created with a Location header built from the Get action's route (api/v1/orders/{id}).
At run time IOrderRepository is EfOrderRepository and INotifier is LoggingNotifier, as registered in AddDonHangInfrastructure.
EfOrderRepository never calls OrderService, and OrderService references no HTTP types.
OrdersController.Get and List call IOrderRepository directly without OrderService; ProductsController and AuthController query DonHangDbContext directly.
With an empty items list, PlaceOrderAsync throws before AddAsync/SaveChangesAsync, and ExceptionHandlingMiddleware maps ArgumentException to 400.
Calls should go down only (HTTP → business → data); calling back up or around a layer spreads a rule over several places.
